| Yield = 5–6 cups
| Difficulty = 3
}}

{{recipe}}| [[Cookbook:Cuisine of France|French cuisine]]

'''''Crème saint-honoré''''' is a ''crème pâtissière'' with stiffly beaten egg whites folded into it, used to fill profiteroles, éclairs and tarts, as well as on its own as a dessert cream. It can be additionally flavoured with liqueur, [[Cookbook:Pralin|''pralin'']], orange peel, etc.

==Ingredients==
* 1 pint [[Cookbook:Crème pâtissière|crème pâtissière]], still hot
* 8 [[Cookbook:Egg White|egg whites]]
* a few drops [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|Tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Superfine Sugar|superfine sugar]] OR [[Cookbook:Granulated Sugar|granulated sugar]]
==Procedure==
# Mix any additional flavourings into the crème pâtissière.
# [[Cookbook:Whipping|Whip]] the egg whites with the salt until soft peaks form.
# Sprinkle the sugar onto the egg whites and continue whipping to stiff peaks.
# [[Cookbook:Mixing#Stirring|Stir]] a quarter of the egg whites into the hot custard.
# [[Cookbook:Folding|Fold]] the rest of the egg whites in and chill before use.
